[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Calculus and Optimization Techniques in Machine Learning"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Calculus and optimization form the mathematical backbone of modern machine learning. Every time a model learns from data, it is fundamentally solving an optimization problem by minimizing a loss function using calculus-based techniques."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"The Role of Derivatives in Model Training"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Derivatives tell us how a function changes when its inputs change. In machine learning, we use partial derivatives to understand how changing a specific weight or bias affects the overall error of the model."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Gradient: A vector of partial derivatives pointing in the direction of the greatest rate of increase of the function."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Loss Function: A mathematical measure of how poorly a model performs on a given task."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Jacobian and Hessian: Higher-order derivatives used for advanced optimization and curvature analysis."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Gradient Descent Optimization"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Gradient descent is an iterative optimization algorithm used to find the minimum of a function. By taking steps proportional to the negative of the gradient, the algorithm converges toward the local minimum of the loss surface."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"import numpy as np

# Simple Gradient Descent for Linear Regression
def gradient_descent(X, y, lr=0.01, epochs=1000):
    m, n = X.shape
    theta = np.zeros(n)
    for _ in range(epochs):
        predictions = np.dot(X, theta)
        errors = predictions - y
        grad = (1/m) * np.dot(X.T, errors)
        theta -= lr * grad
    return theta"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Advanced Optimization Algorithms"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Standard gradient descent can be slow or get stuck in saddle points. Modern machine learning heavily relies on advanced variants that adapt the learning rate dynamically."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD): Computes gradients on small random subsets of data rather than the entire dataset."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Momentum: Helps accelerate SGD in the relevant direction and dampens oscillations by adding a fraction of the previous update."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Adam (Adaptive Moment Estimation): Combines the benefits of AdaGrad and RMSProp, computing adaptive learning rates for each parameter."},{"order":16,"type":"heading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Mastering calculus and optimization allows machine learning practitioners to design better architectures, diagnose training failures, and fine-tune hyperparameters effectively."}]
